p: Watford may be on the edge of London, but it's surrounded by a surprising amount of green space. After a session spent hanging from bars and swinging on ropes, there's nothing better than heading somewhere quiet to cool down.

Whippendell Woods, on the western edge of Cassiobury, is ancient woodland that's gorgeous in spring when the bluebells are out. Croxley Common Moor, close by in Croxley Green, is a nature reserve with open grassland and a peaceful feel. Aldenham Country Park, near Elstree, has a reservoir to walk round, play areas and woodland trails, making it a lovely family afternoon out.
If you'd rather stay closer to town, Watford's High Street and the area around the shopping centre have lots of food choices, so you can refuel quickly after the course.

A few tips: book your ninja slot in advance, especially at weekends, and wear trainers with good grip and comfortable clothes. Keep a snack and drink handy, as a full session can leave you surprisingly hungry. If your crew loves it, a return visit a few weeks later is a great way to see how much they've improved, and nothing beats the look on a child's face when they finally clear the obstacle that beat them last time.
